basis: Fibroblastic neoplasm arising from mesenchymal connective tissue; no additional organ applies across the group.
Cerebral palsy affecting motor control of three limbs; spasticity does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; distal muscle wasting occurs in 7/12 and pes cavus in 7/8. Small testes alone do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Congenital distal joint contractures and foot deformities define this arthrogryposis; facial morphology does not establish another damaged organ.
Congenital cervical vertebral fusion defines Klippel-Feil syndrome. Ocular colobomas are reported, but their frequency in this subtype is unspecified.
Autoinflammatory disease defined by subcutaneous panniculitis and uveitis; unspecified systemic granulomatosis does not establish another organ.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure (28/29) and dysphagia (23/24) reflect respiratory and bulbar muscle weakness, without intrinsic lung or gut disease.
Respiratory motile-cilium dysfunction defines the disease; chronic middle-ear disease with conductive hearing impairment affects over half in typical primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Inherited platelet dysfunction with abnormal bleeding, prolonged bleeding time and possible thrombocytopenia.
Inflammation of the periosteum; infection causes some forms but is not intrinsic to the umbrella concept.
Secondary ischemic necrosis of bone; the underlying cause varies and does not establish a separate vascular or metabolic axis.
Skin nodules, joint contractures/bone lesions and gingival fibromatosis are defining manifestations, despite occasional frequencies for some features in supplied HPO data.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; no extraocular organ involvement is established.
Deficiency of the lectin complement pathway; susceptibility to infections does not establish common lasting damage to a particular organ.
Jaffe-Campanacci syndrome is characterized by multiple nonossifying bone fibromas and persistent cafe-au-lait skin pigmentation; other systemic findings are variable.
Bronchiectasis 6/10, eczema 8/11, scoliosis 6/11 and fractures 4/11 support involvement. Retained primary teeth 9/11 omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Fibroblastic sarcoma of soft connective tissue; later metastases do not justify additional organ labels.
Bacterial infection defined by the organism; no single anatomical site is established across this group.
Burkholderia cepacia syndrome is a fulminant infection characterized by necrotizing pneumonia and sepsis.
Heterotaxy with complex congenital cardiac and vascular malformations. Malrotation frequency is unspecified; situs changes and polysplenia alone do not prove dysfunction.
Progressive tubulointerstitial nephropathy and cholestatic liver disease define the syndrome; an immune mechanism is not established for this specific entity.
Classic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is defined by skin fragility, abnormal scarring and joint hypermobility/dislocations; respiratory symptoms do not prove lasting lung damage.
Rickettsia akari infection; the acute eschar and vesicular eruption generally resolve and do not establish lasting skin damage.
Motor-neuron degeneration causes progressive denervation and muscle wasting: proximal amyotrophy 10/16 and distal amyotrophy 7/16; dysphagia reflects bulbar dysfunction.
Inherited isolated nail dystrophy affecting nail structure; rare autoimmune associations do not establish an immune axis.
